html:
SMTO-CFG-0030 — This Skill doesn't offer that setting or connection test

GUID: e8cacc44-67c3-4887-9c3c-a5708b0bb4e6
Slug: skill-configuration-unsupported
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • You asked to change or test settings for a Skill (an add-on that gives SMTO extra abilities), but the installed version doesn't have them. Nothing was saved or tested.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close the Skill's settings window and reload the SMTO page in your browser. The window may have been opened before the Skill changed, so it can offer options the installed version no longer has.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities and find the Skill. Select the Configure button under its name only if it has one, and use Test connection only if it appears inside those settings. SMTO shows these buttons only for Skills that really provide settings or a connection test.
  3. If you need a setting or test this Skill doesn't offer, ask the person who manages SMTO whether a newer version of the Skill provides it. Only the Skill itself can add these options; SMTO won't treat a test that never ran as a passed test.

What success looks like

  • The Skill's settings open with the fields you expect, or Test connection shows a result message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Skill's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the Skill's connection works just because no test ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Skill configuration route refused the request because the installed Skill declares no installation-level configuration, or its configuration declares no connection-test callback.

What this means

  • The installed Skill has no configuration definition, or its configuration has no declared connection-test implementation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The installed Skill has no configuration definition, or its configuration has no declared connection-test implementation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the installed Skill's actual configuration/test declaration rather than assuming a broken connection.

How to fix it

  • Check the installed Skill's definition: skill.configuration must be non-null for the /api/agent/skills configuration routes, and configuration.test must be set for the configuration/test route. Call only actions advertised by GET configuration (definition.testable) or the capabilities catalog's configurable flag, and upgrade the Skill through its normal installation if the feature is required.
  • Use only configuration fields and connection tests advertised by this installed Skill version. Update the Skill through its normal installation flow if a different capability is required.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Only actions declared by the installed Skill are offered and invoked.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
